kpis.name: Cash runway
kpis.query: Bank + cash journal balances ÷ trailing average monthly fixed operating cost
kpis.formula: Cash today ÷ (payroll + office + software + overhead per month). Months of fixed cost you could cover if revenue stopped.

kpis.name: Cash balance
kpis.query: Σ balances of journals of type bank and cash
kpis.formula: Business cash only. The owner account is tracked separately and never nets into this.

kpis.name: Net profit
kpis.query: Income accounts less direct-cost and overhead accounts, year to date
kpis.formula: Net revenue − direct delivery cost − operating expenses. The plan figure is built from the same three parts, so the gap always decomposes.

kpis.name: Net margin
kpis.query: Net profit ÷ net revenue
kpis.formula: What actually stays in the business per pound invoiced. Plan = gross margin target 44.8% less the 27% overhead ceiling, so the three targets agree with each other.

kpis.name: OPEX ratio
kpis.query: Operating expenses ÷ net revenue
kpis.formula: Overhead as a share of revenue. Rising while gross margin holds means the problem is the office, not delivery.

kpis.name: Revenue at risk
kpis.query: Risk register — expiring retainers + overdue-and-delivering + red projects on top accounts, deduplicated by client
kpis.formula: One number for how much of the revenue base is currently exposed.

kpis.name: Owed to freelancers
kpis.query: Vendor bills of type freelancer with amount_residual > 0, plus approved unbilled hours
kpis.formula: Cash you owe people who have already done the work.

kpis.name: Subscription run-rate
kpis.query: Recurring vendor bills flagged as software subscriptions, monthly equivalent
kpis.formula: Monthly recurring tool cost across the agency.

kpis.name: Freelancer cost ratio
kpis.query: Vendor bills of type freelancer and contractor ÷ net revenue
kpis.formula: How much of every pound invoiced goes straight back out to people who are not on payroll.

kpis.name: Project margin
kpis.query: Project contract value less logged delivery cost, weighted by value
kpis.formula: Blended margin across active and recently closed projects. The delivery half of the margin story; OPEX ratio is the overhead half.

kpis.name: Contracted backlog
kpis.query: Signed sale.order value less amount invoiced to date
kpis.formula: Work already sold and not yet invoiced. Forward cover if nothing new is won.

kpis.name: Net revenue
kpis.query: Posted customer invoice lines excluding media pass-through, by invoice_date
kpis.formula: Invoiced revenue net of media bought on the client's behalf.

kpis.name: Gross margin
kpis.query: (revenue − direct delivery cost) ÷ revenue
kpis.formula: Before overhead. Measures how well work is priced and delivered.

kpis.name: Retainer share
kpis.query: Recurring sale orders ÷ all revenue
kpis.formula: How much of the base is contracted rather than won again each month.

kpis.name: Days sales outstanding
kpis.query: Receivables ÷ (trailing-90 revenue ÷ 90)
kpis.formula: Average days between invoicing and being paid.

kpis.name: Receivables past 60 days
kpis.query: Residual where due date < today−60 ÷ total residual
kpis.formula: The share of the book that is genuinely late.

kpis.name: Collection rate
kpis.query: Payments received ÷ amount falling due in the period
kpis.formula: How much of what fell due this month actually arrived.

kpis.name: Pipeline coverage
kpis.query: Σ(expected revenue × stage probability) ÷ next-quarter new-business target
kpis.formula: How many times over the pipeline covers the target it has to produce.

kpis.name: Win rate
kpis.query: Won ÷ (won + lost) closed in trailing 90 days
kpis.formula: Share of closed opportunities that were won.

kpis.name: Average deal size
kpis.query: Mean contract value of opportunities won in trailing 90 days
kpis.formula: Separates 'we are closing fewer deals' from 'we are closing smaller ones'.

kpis.name: Sales cycle
kpis.query: Mean days from opportunity created to won
kpis.formula: How long money takes to arrive after interest does.

kpis.name: On-time delivery
kpis.query: Tasks with a due date closed on or before it, rolling 30 days
kpis.formula: Deliverables closed by their due date ÷ all deliverables closed.

kpis.name: Overdue tasks
kpis.query: Open tasks where due_date < now
kpis.formula: Work that has already slipped.

kpis.name: Delivered but unbilled
kpis.query: Projects complete > 15 days with no posted invoice
kpis.formula: Work you have done, delivered, and not yet asked to be paid for.

kpis.name: Utilisation
kpis.query: Billable time entries ÷ contracted capacity hours
kpis.formula: Both under- and over-target are penalised: idle capacity costs money, sustained overload costs people.

kpis.name: Attrition · 12 months
kpis.query: Leavers trailing 12 months ÷ average headcount
kpis.formula: Who left, as a share of who there was.

kpis.name: Time to fill
kpis.query: Mean days from requisition opened to offer accepted
kpis.formula: How long a gap in the team stays a gap.

kpis.name: Initiatives on track
kpis.query: Initiatives at green ÷ all active initiatives
kpis.formula: Share of strategic work that is actually moving.

risks.title: Runway below the six-month floor
risks.detail: Cash covers 5.0 months of fixed operating cost against a six-month minimum, while EGP 16,420,000 sits unpaid in receivables and 29.4% of it is already past 60 days.

risks.title: Owner drawings exceeded net profit
risks.detail: EGP 8,900,000 withdrawn year to date against EGP 8,416,200 of net profit. This, plus the receivables build, is the whole cash story.

risks.title: Three clients past 60 days and still in delivery
risks.detail: Cairo Grand (101 days), Zamalek (123) and Alexandria Marine (95) are consuming delivery capacity against unpaid balances.

risks.title: Revenue at risk is nearly half the base
risks.detail: EGP 9,840,000 — 46.2% of trailing-90 revenue — is exposed through expiring retainers, non-paying clients and a red project on the largest account.

risks.title: Coverage well under floor for Q1
risks.detail: Weighted pipeline is 1.22× the Q1 new-business target against a 2.0× floor.

risks.title: Overhead is outgrowing revenue
risks.detail: OPEX ratio 29.4% against a 27% ceiling while gross margin holds near target. The margin leak is overhead, not delivery.

risks.title: On-time delivery under the revised target
risks.detail: 84.1% against the 88% target, with 4 projects red.

risks.title: Attrition above ceiling
risks.detail: 19.4% trailing twelve months against a 15% ceiling, with Design at 92.4% utilisation.

risks.title: Subscription auto-renewal inside 14 days
risks.detail: Adobe Creative Cloud team renews 14 Oct at EGP 62,000/month with 3 of 12 seats unused.

risks.title: Freelancer balances ageing
risks.detail: EGP 1,110,000 of payables past 30 days. Freelancers who wait stop answering.

risks.title: Growth Initiative stalled
risks.detail: No activity for 27 days and the GCC market study is overdue.

risks.title: Delivered but unbilled
risks.detail: 4 completed projects worth EGP 1,680,000 have no invoice after 15 days — cash you have already earned.

decisions.act: Say yes or no to pausing your own drawings.
decisions.title: Cash: pause owner drawings until runway clears six months
decisions.context: Drawings of EGP 8,900,000 against EGP 8,416,200 of profit took more out of the business than it earned. Cash has fallen from EGP 14,280,000 to EGP 9,476,200 in a year when revenue was on plan. Nothing else on this board moves cash as fast as this does.
decisions.impact: Pausing for one quarter adds roughly 1.5 months of cover with no effect on clients, team or delivery. It is the cheapest fix available and entirely within your control.

options.label: Pause drawings for Q4
options.consequence: Cover moves from 5.0 to roughly 6.5 months by 31 Dec. No operational impact.

options.label: Halve drawings for Q4
options.consequence: Cover to roughly 5.8 months. Keeps personal cash flow partly intact.

options.label: Hold drawings, fix cash through collections instead
options.consequence: Depends entirely on Cairo Grand and Zamalek paying. Neither has in three months.

decisions.act: Choose: stop work, hand to legal, or a written payment plan.
decisions.title: Cairo Grand: stop work or escalate to legal
decisions.context: EGP 2,140,000 at 101 days. Work was supposed to pause in August after the leadership sync; two projects are still live and have consumed about 240 hours since.
decisions.impact: Every further month costs roughly EGP 210,000 of delivery capacity against a balance that is now older than the contract's own payment terms.

options.label: Stop all work and issue a formal demand
options.consequence: Maximum leverage. Likely ends a 13.5% revenue line.

options.label: Hand to legal, keep committed deliverables only
options.consequence: Preserves some relationship, starts the clock formally.

options.label: Agree a written payment plan with a hard stop date
options.consequence: Slowest, but the only option that keeps the account.

decisions.act: Cut three unused Adobe seats, then let it renew.
decisions.title: Approve the Adobe renewal, or cut three seats first
decisions.context: Adobe Creative Cloud team auto-renews on 14 October at EGP 62,000/month. Three of twelve seats have had no activity in 90 days.
decisions.impact: Cutting three seats saves roughly EGP 186,000 a year. Doing nothing renews all twelve.

options.label: Hold the renewal and review all tooling

decisions.act: Decide who owns the Horizon renewal — you or Account Management.
decisions.title: Horizon Telecom renewal — contract ends 31 December
decisions.context: An EGP 2.29M trailing-90 account expires in 87 days with no renewal opportunity in Odoo and no owner assigned. It is the second-largest retainer.
decisions.impact: Losing it takes Nile Bank's concentration from 19.4% to roughly 21.6% and removes a tenth of the retainer base.

options.label: Assign to Account Management with a 30-day deadline
options.consequence: Standard path, but AM has no permanent head.

options.label: Let it lapse and redeploy capacity
options.consequence: Frees roughly 90 hours a month, worsens concentration.

decisions.act: Tell Finance to invoice the four finished projects.
decisions.title: Bill the four completed-but-uninvoiced projects this week
decisions.context: Four projects marked complete in ClickUp more than 15 days ago have no Odoo invoice. EGP 1,680,000 of work already delivered.
decisions.impact: Invoicing today puts the cash roughly 45 days closer. It is the fastest money on this board and needs no client negotiation.

options.label: Invoice all four this week
options.consequence: Adds EGP 1.68M to receivables now, cash in ~45 days.

options.label: Review scope on two of them first
options.consequence: Delays two invoices by a week; protects against disputes.

decisions.act: Approve or freeze the two backfill roles.
decisions.title: Q4 hiring freeze on the two open non-critical roles
decisions.context: Three roles are open. Two are backfills with no client commitment attached; one is the Senior Performance Marketer the Performance function depends on.
decisions.impact: Freezing the two backfills protects roughly EGP 1.4M of annualised payroll while runway is under four months. It also raises load on teams already at 85%+ utilisation.

options.label: Freeze the two backfills, keep the Performance hire
options.consequence: Protects cash, keeps the committed capability.

options.label: Freeze all three
options.consequence: Maximum cash protection, stalls the Performance build.

options.label: Proceed with all three
options.consequence: Keeps capacity, costs roughly EGP 1.4M annualised against a tight runway.
